quality.execution_tail_policy: Emit decisions after warm-up including all last-horizon states; future target availability only restricts training and classification metrics.

signal_policy.description: Predicted up requests long; down/unchanged requests flat. After the configured maximum consecutive long decisions, force one flat target before another long request.
signal_policy.limitation: This cap is a decision rule, not an execution holding-time guarantee. Pending IOC orders and segment-end unresolved inventory remain explicit simulator limitations. Execution decisions include the unlabelled last-horizon states.

warnings: One venue/instrument and fixed two-hour excerpts per selected date; results do not establish continuous-day or cross-market generalization.
Date-block uncertainty remains conditional on dependence/stationarity assumptions; shared expanding fits may induce longer dependence.
Macro-F1 uses all three fixed classes; balanced accuracy averages classes present on each true evaluation date.
Classification evidence is not evidence of executable profit. Economic results require the separate declared simulator and costs.
Local signals and fitted models are excluded from published aggregate artifacts.

aggregate.capital_convention: Each observed segment independently starts with initial_cash and zero inventory. PnL is summed across independent cases, not a continuous investable equity curve.
aggregate.annualization: Not computed. No annualized Sharpe, compounded annual return or fabricated gap equity.
aggregate.inventory_convention: Unclosed spot inventory is marked at the final observed best bid, not liquidated through a gap.

assumptions.accounting: Spot quote-currency cash and base-quantity long/flat inventory only; no inverse, leverage, shorting, funding or borrowing.
assumptions.inference_delay: Signals are available exactly at their matched source receipt timestamp; execution latency represents the declared action delay.
assumptions.zero_latency: A strictly later source event is always required; a tied receipt microsecond is eligible only when source_order is later.
assumptions.pending_policy: Keep first pending order; record subsequent signals as ignored until its attempt or segment-end cancellation.
assumptions.execution: One marketable IOC consumes each displayed side level at most once in the execution observation. Cancel unfilled remainder immediately; no passive/queue/fill-probability claims.
assumptions.historical_book: Each later observed snapshot replaces displayed liquidity. Own orders do not alter the historical feed; no endogenous market-impact feedback is modeled.
assumptions.quote_age: execution receive_time_us minus exchange event_time_us; reject negative clock skew and age above max_quote_age_us.
assumptions.rounding: Target/fill quantities round down to quantity_step. Adverse buy prices round up and sell prices down to price_tick.
assumptions.fees: Charge fee_bps on actual execution notional exactly in Decimal quote units. Venue-specific fee/minimum-charge rounding is not modeled.
assumptions.cash_limits: Affordable buy quantities include fees and are rounded down; no negative cash or excess base exposure.
assumptions.segments: Each declared source/date/segment is an independent case starting with initial_cash and zero inventory. No gap liquidity or continuous annual equity is fabricated.
assumptions.segment_end: Cancel pending orders and mark unclosed inventory at the last observed best bid; no unobserved liquidation fill.
assumptions.gross_pnl: Net marked PnL plus fees; adverse execution/slippage remains included. Zero-cost replay is a separate diagnostic.
assumptions.gap_detection: Segment identifiers come from upstream normalization/window selection; absent disconnect events cannot be reconstructed here.
assumptions.redistribution: Orders, fills, ledger, signal events and per-segment detail remain local. Export aggregate metrics/hashes only.

paper.title: Queue Imbalance as a One-Tick-Ahead Price Predictor in a Limit Order Book
paper.idea: Predict the binary next nonzero midpoint move using opposing top-queue imbalance.
paper.original_market: 10 Nasdaq stocks during 2014 using LOBSTER data

differences_from_paper: Bitstamp BTCUSD spot on newly selected fixed date/window excerpts, rather than the paper's equity data.
One causal decision at each constant-midpoint run start instead of random within-run clock-time sampling.
Expanding earlier-date development fits instead of a randomized train/test partition.
Fixed C=1 regularized logistic with train-only scaling instead of unpenalized global logistic fitting.
No local-logistic variant, paper sample-size matching or claimed match to published numerical tables.

quality.decision_sampling: first observation of each constant-midpoint run, excluding the terminal run
quality.target: binary direction of next observed nonzero midpoint change inside the same segment
quality.midpoint_representation: integer half-tick units on the declared price grid

queue_logistic.log_loss_endpoint_policy: sklearn machine-epsilon clipping for probabilities exactly zero or one
